source.quote: FiiO's own parameters page, read 2026-11-24. « Hardware solution »: « DAC: ES9039SPRO*2; USB: XMOS XU316; Bluetooth decoding: QCC5125; AMP: 8-way THX788+ ». Rate rows: « USB decoding: supports up to 768kHz/32bit; DSD512 (Native)；MQA »; « Coaxial input decoding: supports up to 192kHz/24bit; DSD64 »; « Optical input decoding: supports up to 96kHz/24bit ». The same block also contains « Coaxial output: supports up to 192kHz/24bit; DSD64 », « Optical fiber output: supports up to 192kHz/24bit », « HDMI decoding: supports up to 192kHz/24bit », « HDMI output: supports up to 192kHz/24bit » and « HDMI ARC decoding: supports 44.1/48kHz ». No filter, oversampling, NOS or DSD-mode row. Nothing about R2R, ladder or delta-sigma; only the chip name.

facts.chip: Two ES9039SPRO (ESS), XMOS XU316 as USB receiver, QCC5125 for Bluetooth, « 8-way THX788+ » amplifier.

_lhdmi_nest_PAS_ecrit_et_la_raison_est_l: « HDMI decoding: supports up to 192kHz/24bit » and « HDMI ARC decoding: supports 44.1/48kHz » both appear, and the reader who collected these rows said the grouping of this part of the block « is not fully certain because the indicator legend is interleaved » - that is, it could not establish which rows are inputs and which are outputs. Only the three rows the page labels « input decoding » are written. An HDMI ceiling at 44.1/48 kHz would be the lowest in the catalogue after McIntosh's MCT and is exactly the kind of figure worth having; it is left out because a doubt about which column a number belongs to is a doubt about the number.
